von Weizsacker, E. U., Hargroves, K. C., Smith, M. H., Desha, C. and Stasinopoulos, P. (2009). Factor Five: Transforming the Global Economy through 80% Improvements in Resource Productivity. A Report to the Club of Rome. Earthscan, London. Chapter 1 only: "A Framework for Factor Five" (The Natural Edge Project), 38-page free chapter extract.

BACKGROUND - NO TECHNOLOGY DATA. Chapter 1 of Factor Five is a framework chapter (whole-system design, resource productivity, Factor Four case-study recap, decoupling, rebound). It prints only aggregate claims: industrial processes at least 50% more energy-intensive than necessary; generation efficiency 25-45%; T&D about 91% efficient; boilers 70-80% (up to about 90%) fuel conversion efficiency; 20% saving in each of ten steps leaves 11%; geopolymer cement "at least 80 per cent less energy intensity" than Portland cement, deferred to Chapter 3. UKERC: one UKERC row group credits "Von Weizsacker 2009" (C-CS3 E-crete / Zeobond geopolymer, with Duxson 2007 and NBF 2007): capital and O&M costs per t cement and energy. Chapter 1 cannot support those numbers - it has no costs and its 80% energy claim is a pointer to Chapter 3 (the cement sector study), which is not held. The UKERC citation most likely rests on Chapter 3. The helper lists no UKERC rows for this id, so no recon file was written. Printed page numbers run from p.1; PDF = 38 pages.
